content.thinking: With no changes and no logs to point to, the alert itself is clearly describing state-divergence, so that's the answer.

hypotheses.subject: cached spend totals
hypotheses.summary: The cached per-shopper spend totals stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger around 2026-10-18T16:38:00Z. The ledger is correct and only the cache copies are stale, so this is state divergence. Nothing was deployed or flagged to cause it, and nothing refreshes an entry once its shopper buys again.

supporting_evidence.claim: 90 of 240 cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind; the oldest unaccounted purchase was recorded at 2026-10-18T16:38:00Z, which is when the copies stopped keeping up.
get_changes returned: nothing changed from 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-18T19:37:13Z
The metrics show no departure from baseline in any series, which fits stale values being served without errors or latency.
All three pods are on Tesla-V100 nodes and started at 07:37:13Z, before the divergence began, so there is no placement change.
